title: The Sharp Deadline
premise: Jonah Quintana's quiet life of guarded secrets shatters when a woman named Mara Voss repays a favor he never did — saving his estranged brother from a cartel hit years ago — by demanding he hand over the encrypted ledger he's been hiding for his dirtiest client, media mogul Aldous Crane. The ledger contains proof that Crane ordered the murder of a journalist, and both the cartel and Crane's private army will burn cities to bury it. As Jonah and Mara run, they gather a ragtag crew of people he once protected but never trusted, discovering the found family he'd refused to believe in. In the end Jonah trades the ledger to Crane in exchange for his brother's life, then detonates the real bomb: a duplicate already seeded across newsrooms worldwide, toppling Crane while costing Jonah everything except the people who stayed.
about_author: Hazel Eastwick is a former insurance fraud investigator who spent a decade reading other people's lies before she started writing her own. She lives off-grid on the Maine coast with two rescue dogs and an unhealthy knowledge of lock-picking.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. We meet him mid-job guarding a paranoid tech executive, establishing his rules: no attachments, bag always packed, one polished lie about his past ready at all times. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Mara Voss corners Jonah in a diner, claiming he owes her for saving his brother Danny from a cartel execution — a debt on a favor he never asked for. She wants the Crane ledger within seventy-two hours. POV: Jonah. Beat: the floor drops out of his orderly life.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Holds
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter as Jonah recalls how he came to possess Crane's encrypted ledger during a botched extraction in Bogotá. POV: Jonah. Beat: dread deepens — we learn it proves Crane ordered journalist Elena Ruiz's murder.

chapters.title: Crane's Smile
chapters.summary: Aldous Crane summons Jonah for a routine briefing that is anything but; Crane hints he knows someone is circling the ledger. POV: alternating Jonah and a brief Crane section. Beat: cat-and-mouse begins, menace wrapped in charm.

chapters.title: Danny
chapters.summary: Jonah tracks down his estranged brother, who confirms Mara's story is true — and that the cartel has resumed hunting him. POV: Danny. Beat: guilt and old wounds; family as liability and lifeline.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Jonah decides to steal the ledger back from his own dead-drop rather than give it to either side, contacting former colleague Priya Nair, a fixer he once burned. POV: Jonah. Beat: first act of open rebellion against every rule he lives by.

chapters.title: The Dead-Drop Job
chapters.summary: Tense heist chapter: Jonah and Priya retrieve the ledger from a storage unit under surveillance. They barely escape Crane's security chief, Rook. POV: Priya. Beat: adrenaline and grudging trust forming.

chapters.title: Rook Closes In
chapters.summary: Rook interrogates Crane's staff and identifies Mara, putting a tail on her. POV: Rook. Beat: cold institutional menace; power shown as machinery, not passion.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Jonah, Mara, Priya, and Danny hole up in a safehouse; alliances fray over what to do with the ledger — sell it, leak it, or use it as leverage. POV: Mara. Beat: found family's messy birth; arguments that feel like intimacy.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Mara reveals her full history: Elena Ruiz was her sister, and she engineered the 'debt' to recruit the one man with access to Crane. POV: Mara. Beat: betrayal inside the betrayal — but also raw grief that reframes everything.

chapters.title: Compromised
chapters.summary: Rook's team hits the safehouse; the group scatters into the city during a rain-soaked chase. Danny is captured. POV: Jonah. Beat: panic, failure, the cost of trusting too late.

chapters.title: Terms of Trade
chapters.summary: Crane offers Jonah a deal: the ledger for Danny's life, plus a clean exit. Jonah pretends to consider while Priya traces Rook's operational pattern. POV: Jonah. Beat: moral vertigo — the devil's offer is genuinely tempting.

chapters.title: Cartel Interlude
chapters.summary: The Serrano cartel, owed its own debt, intercepts the exchange plans and demands the ledger as tribute instead. POV: cartel lieutenant Tomás. Beat: third force raises stakes; everyone is someone's asset.

chapters.title: Priya's Ledger
chapters.summary: Priya decrypts a second layer of the file: Crane's network extends into law enforcement and a senator. Leaking it means burning innocent bystanders too. POV: Priya. Beat: truth revealed as double-edged; loyalty vs. truth crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Quiet character chapter before the storm: rooftop conversations, confessions, Jonah admitting the lie he's polished for years is that he doesn't care. POV: rotating short sections. Beat: tenderness under countdown pressure.

chapters.title: Three-Way Meeting
chapters.summary: Jonah brokers a meeting with Crane, Rook, and Tomás at a freight terminal, planning to play each against the others while Priya runs the leak remotely. POV: Jonah. Beat: high-wire tension; his con-man skills finally serve something good.

chapters.title: Terminal Firefight
chapters.summary: The meeting collapses; Rook turns on Tomás, gunfire erupts, and Jonah trades the real ledger to Crane under duress to save Danny. POV: Jonah. Beat: sacrifice and apparent defeat — he hands over the secret worth killing for.

chapters.title: Everything Burns Downward
chapters.summary: Crane discovers the delivered drive is poisoned malware that wipes his empire's records and triggers the seeded duplicates. Newsrooms worldwide receive Elena's file. POV: Crane. Beat: corrupt power devouring itself; fury and unraveling.

chapters.title: Rook's Last Contract
chapters.summary: Rook, disavowed, hunts the group for revenge rather than payment; Mara takes a bullet shielding Danny. POV: Mara. Beat: loyalty proven in blood; the found family holds its line.

chapters.title: The Sharp Deadline
chapters.summary: Climax: Jonah confronts Crane atop his headquarters as federal agents close in, offering him the only mercy left — testimony in exchange for naming names. Crane refuses and falls, literally and figuratively. POV: Jonah. Beat: truth wins, but not cleanly.

chapters.title: Aftermath Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Weeks later: congressional hearings, Mara recovering, Danny sober and present, Priya rebuilding her career. Jonah unpacks the go-bag for the first time in years. POV: Jonah. Beat: grief settling into gratitude.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: Epilogue: the group shares a cramped Thanksgiving dinner in Mara's apartment; Jonah gets a new job offer and declines it, choosing the people over the paycheck. Final image: the go-bag repurposed as a diaper bag for Danny's daughter. POV: Jonah. Beat: home, at last, chosen not stumbled into.
